title: Platform playbook: systems & services runbooks, dashboards, alerts, and roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Ava Martinez
summary:
Canonical playbook for the Platform Systems & Services team: inventory, owners, SLOs, dashboards, alerting guidance, runbooks, how-tos, retro cadence, and Q1

Q3 2026 roadmap priorities.
content:
Introduction

This playbook collects operational guidance for Redwood's Platform Systems & Services team. It covers the systems inventory, owners, SLOs, Grafana dashboards and panels, Prometheus alerting guidance and example rules, on-call runbooks for common incidents, standard how-tos for routine changes, retrospective cadence and postmortem expectations, and the near-term roadmap through Q3 2026. Audience: platform engineers, SRE, on-call responders, and service owners.

Service inventory and ownership

- k8s-control (eng-platform) — Owner: Marcus Lee — Pager: oncall-eng-platform — Slack: #platform-k8s
- rds-scheduler (eng-platform) — Owner: Priya Nair — Pager: oncall-eng-platform — Slack: #platform-scheduler
- inference-proxy (eng-serving-runtime) — Owner: Diego Alvarez — Pager: oncall-serving-runtime — Slack: #serving-runtime
- kv-cache (eng-platform) — Owner: Zob Kim — Pager: oncall-storage — Slack: #platform-cache
- monitoring-stack (eng-sre) — Owner: Samir Patel — Pager: oncall-sre — Slack: #sre-monitoring

Service-level objectives (SLOs) summary

- k8s-control: API P95 < 120ms, monthly availability 99.95%
- rds-scheduler: job scheduling P95 < 250ms, availability 99.9%
- inference-proxy: p95 tail latency < 120ms (dedicated tier), error rate < 0.5%
- kv-cache: cache hit rate > 85%, eviction rate < 0.3%

Dashboards (canonical Grafana)

- Platform Overview (platform-overview-001): cluster capacity, pod start time, CPU/GPU utilization, latency heatmap
- Control Plane Health (k8s-control-002): apiserver QPS, etcd latency, scheduler queue depth
- Inference Gateway (inference-proxy-003): request rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, 5m error rate, connections by region
- Cache & Batching (kv-cache-004): hit rate, batch size distribution, eviction metrics
- Monitoring Stack (monitoring-stack-005): scrape health, alerts firing, TSDB retention

Dashboard ownership: owners listed above must maintain panel descriptions and add an "Actionable threshold" note for panels used by alerts.

Alerting guidance and examples

Principles: alert on customer-visible symptoms, avoid noisy low-value alerts, use aggregation windows and composite alerts, include runbook links, and classify severity (Sev0-Sev3).

Example Prometheus rules (illustrative):
- Sev0: InferenceProxyHighErrorRate
  expr: sum(rate(inference_proxy_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_proxy_requests_total[5m])) > 0.02
  for: 3m
  labels: severity=critical, service=inference-proxy
  annotations: summary="Inference proxy error rate > 2% (5m)", runbook="/confluence/eng-platform/inference-proxy-runbook"

- Sev1: K8sControlAPIHighP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le)) > 0.12
  for: 10m
  labels: severity=high, service=k8s-control

- Sev2: KVCacheLowHitRate
  expr: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate[15m]) < 0.75
  for: 15m
  labels: severity=medium, service=kv-cache

How-tos (procedures)

Add an alert rule
1) Validate symptom and SLO impact with service owner and SRE.
2) Implement rule in monitoring-rules repo (branch: alert/<service>-<short-desc>).
3) Add rationale, SLO impact, test queries, and notification routing to the PR.
4) Run CI lint and dry-run.
5) Merge and observe for 30
minutes with owner.

Scale node pool (manual)
1) Verify unschedulable pods and cluster utilization on Platform Overview.
2) Inspect autoscaler: kubectl describe hpa -n platform.
3) Terraform change: cd infra/cluster && terraform plan -var='node_count=NEW_COUNT' && terraform apply.
4) Announce on #platform-ops and monitor pod startup latency.
5) Rollback if pod start latency > 5x baseline or SLOs degrade.

Runbooks (incident playbooks)

Inference-proxy high error rate (Sev0/Sev1)
- Symptoms: 5m error rate > 2% OR p95 > 300ms for 5m
- First responder checklist:
  1) Acknowledge in PagerDuty, create #incident-<id>, and join bridge.
  2) Open Inference Gateway dashboard (last 15m) and capture rate/latency/error breakdowns.
  3) Check recent rollouts: kubectl get deploy -n serving && kubectl describe deploy inference-proxy.
  4) If rollout present, rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-proxy -n serving.
  5) Check pod resource usage and OOMs: kubectl top pods -n serving; kubectl get events -n serving.
  6) If network to runtime failing, validate routes and NAT gateway; escalate to eng-infra.
  7) If unresolved in 30 minutes, escalate to eng-serving-runtime and start postmortem process.

Etcd high commit latency (k8s-control Sev1)
- Symptoms: etcd p99 > 1s for 10m
- Steps: check disk IO (iostat), verify compaction and backups, failover reads and replace node if disk saturated.

Retrospectives and postmortems

- Fast retro: 30

60 minutes within 7 days for Sev1/Sev0
- Deep postmortem: 90

120 minutes for Sev0 with >30m customer impact

Postmortem template: summary and timeline, root cause with evidence, corrective actions with owner and due date, preventative actions, verification plan.

Roadmap (near-term priorities)

Q1 2026:
- Migrate dashboards to Grafana v8 shared instance and deduplicate panels
- Implement composite alerts for inference-proxy to reduce noise
- Begin autoscaler improvements for model onboarding bursts

Q2 2026:
- Deploy prefix KV caching telemetry and adaptive batching visibility
- Roll out low-latency tracing sampling for tail analysis
- Harden and automate etcd recovery playbooks

Q3 2026:
- Add cost signals (token cost / per-model unit economics) to Platform Overview
- Publish self-service runbook templates and oncall handover docs in the team wiki

Team wiki and resources

- Monitoring rules repo: git@github.com:redwood/monitoring-rules
- Infra repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-cluster
- Oncall schedule: https://oncall.redwood.com/eng-platform
- Runbook templates: /confluence/eng-platform/runbook-templates

Oncall rotation and escalation policy

- Primary: eng-platform weekly rotation. Secondary: eng-sre 24/7 backup.
- Escalation timeline: acknowledge within 5 minutes, escalate to secondary after 10 minutes with no progress, start Sev0 bridge after 30 minutes if unresolved.

Change management and maintenance

- Any SLO-affecting change requires a runbook update and short risk assessment.
- Playbook owner must review quarterly and update reviewers list after major changes.

Appendices

- Alert annotation keys required: summary, runbook, playbook
- CLI cheat sheet: kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide; kubectl get events -n serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp; kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n <ns>
- Runbook YAML frontmatter template for programmatic linking: title, service, owner, severity
